Synopsis:
    NY Fed President John Williams attributes rising long-term bond yields to a strong US economy and AI/tech investment, not inflation fears. With the fed funds rate at 3.5–3.75%, a hike is widely expected at the Sept 15–16 FOMC meeting. Williams signals data-dependency and caution, noting tariffs and the Middle East conflict as key inflation drivers. He frames the rate decision as complex, offers no pre-commitment, but acknowledges persistence of above-target inflation. Fed Chair Warsh has also signaled willingness to act if needed. Treasury yield management is seen as non-disruptive to monetary policy.
